record.text: Spider-Man Brand New Day comes closer to my ideal of what an MCU film should be like than any entry in the franchise since Endgame. Like a good run of comics all smooshed into two and a half hours.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a great movie that dives in the Peter Parker’s loneliness and how isolating yourself from those who care will only hurt you. Despite so many characters and plot developments, the movie doesn’t become a disjointed mess. This is Tom Holland’s best Spider-Man. Recommend.

record.text:
Spider-man Brand New Day is... good.

Solid script, SUPER bloated, at times feels like a 2h trailer for future movies, and I'm kinda angry about one thing that I don't think belongs in a Spider-Man movie, but... 

...they did it really well, so it's hard to be mad about it. Kind of admire it, even

I get the appeal but before you spend money on Spider-Man Brand New Day, you should know Spidey acts like those cops who use Flock cameras to track down someone they're stalking. This is not an exaggeration. He uses facial recog on all the NYC cameras to find a woman. The film is NORMALIZING that.

To put Spider-Man: Brand New Day into words would do it a disservice, but here’s my attempt:

It was spectacular. An emotional journey, full of laughs, depth, incredible visuals and an unbelievable performance from Tom Holland.

If you were even considering it, watch it.

images.alt:
After the record-breaking global success of Spider-Man: No Way Home, Spider-Man:
Brand New Day marks an entirely new chapter for Peter Parker and Spider-Man.
Four years have passed since the events of No Way Home, and Peter is now an adult living entirely alone, having voluntarily erased himself from the lives and memories of those he loves. Crime-fighting in a New York that no longer knows his name, he's devoted himself entirely to protecting his city - a full-time Spider-Man - but as the demands on him intensify, the pressure sparks a surprising physical evolution that threatens his existence, even as a strange new pattern of crimes gives rise to one of the most powerful threats he has ever faced.

73. Spider-Man: Brand New Day

Although the pacing of the film’s plot can move a bit too slow at times, this is the most mature and lived in that Spider-Man’s world has felt before, concerned with its characters and their internal lives that previous live action films have never fully explored.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day

On paper, this is juggling a lot but aside from one character, its honestly handled pretty well. The focus is still on Peter's arc which is really well handled and the general presentation compared to the previous Holland movies is much improved

images.alt:
After the record-breaking global success of Spider-Man: No Way Home, Spider-Man:
Brand New Day marks an entirely new chapter for Peter Parker and Spider-Man.
Four years have passed since the events of No Way Home, and Peter is now an adult living entirely alone, having voluntarily erased himself from the lives and memories of those he loves. Crime-fighting in a New York that no longer knows his name, he's devoted himself entirely to protecting his city - a full-time Spider-Man - but as the demands on him intensify, the pressure sparks a surprising physical evolution that threatens his existence, even as a strange new pattern of crimes gives rise to one of the most powerful threats he has ever faced.

record.text:

record.text: Spider-Man: Brand New Day is... kind of all over the place.  There are definitely some good ideas in there, lots of them, but the execution is mixed.  It's heavier than the other MCU spider flicks and Cretton's direction is less fun than Watts' for better or worse.

Spider Man brand new day is a dark, morose story of the pain of needing to escalate versus the need to evolve.

It’s well made but it is so dour and obsessed with sickness / illness / fatigue / grief that it forgets the one thing Spidey movies most rely on: it’s not fun, like, at all.

record.text: Happy Spider-Man Day! To celebrate I watched Spider-Man Brand New Day and Absolutely Loved it! 🥹🕷️❤️

images.alt: Spider-man seated upside down on a metal beam, the city skyline placed on top of the frame. He's looking at his phone unmasked.

It’s been a while since the last one but I’ve always appreciated how Spidey movies balance heart with the spectacle. And to be clear, the spectacle in this one is wonderfully designed fight scenes w/ weight & impact. I care about these characters so much and just want the best for them. They’re compelling even in just simple dialogue scenes with each other.  

I also loved looking at this movie! I love how lived in scenes felt with the frame crammed with details and people. Like Pluribus, this film understands that the way people move unnaturally is cinematic. The specific way Scorpion fights with his tail that acts like another limb is badass! 
While I could take or leave its connections to the greater MCU, I too struggle with the tech our hero uses. Feels too normalizing of surveillance tech and it’s not a good look.   

Spidey has always felt the most human, the most vulnerable and I’m so glad DDC and crew capture that and give us so many glimpses of the lives of the people in our hero’s care.

items.alt: The first Sam Raimi Spider-Man is flawed, but a damn good comic book movie!! The cast is perfect, especially Willem Dafoe as Green Goblin, the origin story is handled very well, and while it takes liberties like organic webbing and some of the dialogue is hokey, its still a great time to have. If not for this, we wouldn't have the comic book movies we have today!

Really the only "Spider-Man" movie I don't like. I'm a defender of Andrew Garfield's first TASM movie, it has it's issues for sure, but I thought it was a good starting point. But aside from cool effects and Garfield & Stone's amazing chemistry, this is so cluttered, so stupid, the story is nonsensical, and it's just a forced way to start a cinematic universe which this was the springboard for it, and failed miserably

Andrew Garfield deserves a better movie, and while I loved his return in No Way Home, that doesn't give this movie a pass for screwing him over out of getting a proper trilogy and being AWFUL!! The Amazing Spider-Man 2 sucks, nuff' said.

Before this movie, I didn't even know who Miles Morales was... AND BY GOD, WHAT AN INTRODUCTION!! This movie has such a rich plot about Miles being roped into being Spider-Man after his Spider-Man kicked the can, and what better way for him to learn from than, well... other Spider Variants?

Miles is such a fun character, you root for him on his journey, and he stands abive all the challenges he faces and proves why he IS Spider-Man!! There is literally nothing else I can add about this movie, I love it to death, and it's just a spectacular movie!!

WHY THE FUCK IS THIS SO DAMN HATED?!?!

"Oh Mysterio is an Iron Man villain-" doesn't stop him from being a fun, cool, tripping as hell villain, who is played so wonderfully by Jake Gyllenhaal. And as Mysterio is my favorite SSpider-Man villain if all time, I could care less about "oh he's an Iron Man villain, wah wah wah"

"Oh it doesn't take place in New York-" okay so fucking what? Parker goes on a vacation with his class after the hell that was Infinity War and Endgame. How is that a genuine problem?

"Why would Stark give Parker glasses with dangerous tech-" it's pretty fucking clear that throughout their time together, Tony saw Peter as the son he never had, and wanted him to be the hero he saw in him. Keep in mind, THIS IS LITERALLY AFTER ENDGAME, AND HIS DEATH IS STILL FRESH IN PETER'S MIND!! Stark wanted Peter to be okay even after he was gone, and I find that so heartwarming that he trusted Peter as he did with Rhodey, Pepper, and Happy

I don't care what anybody fucking says, Spider-Man: Far From Home is goated as hell, and no amount of crybaby chronically online bitches that say otherwise will stop me from loving it. It's a good, fun, summer movie and a nice epilogue of Endgame. Go watch this movie, I guarantee you it's amazing!

The movie that's a love letter to every live action iteration of Spider-Man that has graced the big-screen!

What more can I say about No Way Home that hasn't been said? It's emotional, it's characters are fun, the return of iconic villains is great, and seeing Tobey and Andrew come back... one of my top movie theater moments of all freaking time!! And with how this movie ends, Peter Parker makes the until sacrifice that makes him fully embrace and become the depressed & street level Spider-Man he is in the comics! 

I still love Homecoming and Far Frome Home, but No Way Home does deserve the crown of being the best in the Jon Watts trilogy. And it leads into... a brand new day, 👀

When the movie's climax has a Pepsi sign kill the fucking forgettable villain, and has acting on the levels of Tommy Wiseau's The Room... what the fuck was Sony thinking about this spin-off verse?

With the exception of Let There Be Carnage, (which to me is just fun cuz it's great seeing Carnage) this whole universe was doomed and fundamentally flawed from the start. People want to see the characters AS VILLAINS FOR SPIDER-MAN!! They don't want to see them as boring "anti-heroes" that would have no reason to fucking fight him. Thank God this universe is dead and buried. 

If you wanna know how bad this was, just read interviews with Dakota Johnson about this movie. The poor woman was tricked thinking it was an MCU movie she was staring in, not a shitty Sony Villain Movie. Don't waste your time on this, Morbius, Kraven, and the Venom movies... maybe give Let The Be Carnage a shot with how dumb fun it is, but fuck the rest

I'm being genuine when I say that Spider-Man: Brand New Day is the best live action Spider-Man movie period. 

It is like seeing the comic panels of Stan Lee and Steve Ditko come to life as this movie has such a heartwrenching, rich, emotional story, and is why Tom Holland is the absolute BEST Spider-Man actor of all time. I dare not say anything else, please go see Brand New Day!! It's amazing, superior, ultimate and spectacular!!

record.text: Spider-Man: Brand New Day was so good! What a great way to do a soft reboot and still carry a ton of continuity. 🕷️ 🕸️

I enjoyed Spider-Man: Brand New Day. It was more serious, even somber at times, and traded the usual big-bad formula for something more nuanced. Destin Daniel Cretton (who directed the excellent Shang-Chi movie) built the story around its characters, and the result felt refreshingly grounded.

Spider-Man: Brand New Day really did resonate with me on many emotional and personal levels that I actually felt a lot of emotions that made me feel something, given that it tells a human and relatable story about Peter Parker going through his depression and loneliness which I related to him.

A colorful four-panel collage features scenes labeled for days of the week. 
-The Monday panel shows a young woman with long brown hair wearing a gray coat and white shirt, clinging to Spider-Man in his red and blue suit against a soft cityscape background, both looking tense and alert. 
-The Tuesday panel depicts Olivier Queen from Smallville, a blond, rugged man with a dirty, bloodied face in a dimly lit room, aiming a pistol straight ahead with an intense, determined expression. 
- The Wednesday panel features Subamrimon, an animated robotic narwhal-like creature with a large silver drill for a horn, a white and purple body, yellow fin-like ears, and teal eyes, standing in a metallic hallway. 
- The Thursday panel shows an anime-style close-up of a framed photo being held of Usagi and Mamoru from the 90’s Sailor Moon; the picture inside shows a blonde girl with twin buns and pigtails in a school uniform sitting close to a dark-haired young man in a pink shirt and gray pants, both looking happy and peaceful.

record.text:
Spider-Man: Brand New Day
This was great. I honestly love how much more character-driven Tom Holland's Spiderman is compared to the past takes. I also love the banter between him and Punisher, they were great fun to watch arguing LOL

One thing I appreciate about Spider-Man: Brand New Day is in its not dotting every ‘I’ and crossing every ‘T’. There’s room for people to debate the meaning of one scene or another, and that’s a good thing.

With the release of Spider-Man: Brand New Day, my fellow Line it is Drawn artists and I got to take famous movie posters and make them spider themed. Here's my take on the Wayans Brothers' comedy White Chicks.

So yeah. SPIDER-MAN: BRAND NEW DAY is not THE DARK KNIGHT. Not unrelated, 2026 is not 2008. We DO sustain a far more broad and deep assault on our privacy now than we did then. And, you know, our world doesn't even have Skrulls and shit.

images.alt:
REVIEW: Spider-Man: Brand New Day

It's hard to know where to begin on this one given that digging even a little into the plot necessitates wading into the dreaded spoiler territory for what turns out to be two substantial twists, one medium-sized that I worked out about ten minutes in and one JUMBO that I thankfully never saw coming. The good news is that a) both are handled well, with ample setup and payoff and without any lame false leads or cheats, and b) this approach is quite refreshing for a series like Spider-Man and allows for some interesting performances and character turns. And the action is pretty damn good too, but you shouldn't need me to tell you that.

Is it as good as the first two Raimi films? Not quite, no. Am I coming out of it as excited for Doomsday as I was for Infinity War? Not by a long shot, but I've more or less accepted that's down to that particular hype cycle being lightning in a bottle and the fact that I'm just getting older. Brand New Day is still a winner, and makes the strongest case in awhile for keeping both this series and the broader Marvel train rolling. Recommended.

Rating: 8/10.

It seems inevitable that Tom Holland is gonna keep doing this at least a while longer (it helps that he's one of those guys that somehow looks exactly 22 no matter how old he actually is 😆), but I can't not observe that it feels like we're well beyond due for a live-action Miles Morales film. Maybe that's in the cards post-Doomsday? 🤔

Four years of silence ends the way Doctor Strange's spell always promised it would — brutally. Spider-Man: Brand New Day doesn't just bring Peter Parker back into focus; it puts him through a rebirth that costs him almost everything he has left, and this is our full spoiler breakdown of exactly how. If Brand New Day is ultimately a movie about the importance of a healthy work-life balance, it doesn’t always find the right equilibrium. To begin with, its preoccupation with solitude renders it deficient in the zippy ensemble comedy that has long been the MCU’s stealthiest asset. Nor does it fully exploit Holland’s gawky charm or Zendaya’s willowy grace. To be sure, it delivers two very good scenes between Peter and MJ: one set on a rooftop against the night sky, when a seemingly cathartic kiss is revealed to be a dastardly feint; the other in a nondescript interior, where the characters’ feelings spill out in a mix of anger, hunger, and sorrow. But on the whole, the film operates as a kind of emotional placeholder, deferring any resolution or progression of its relationships to a subsequent installment.

images.alt:
4 out of 5
This movie was a blast from start to finish. I felt like a kid in my seat watching Spider-Man on the big screen for the first time again.
This movie really does feel like a fresh start despite being a sequel. It feels like a new story is beginning with loose threads to the original trilogy in the best way.
The movie itself has some incredible action that is so obviously Destin Daniel Cretton's work. The camerawork in some key scenes is phenomenal.
While the script is a bit predictable and the movie's length was felt a little, it wasn't bad enough to ruin the movie for me, I'll definitely be going back an rewatching. The script and Tom Holland did incredible job's at conveying how Peter is feeling throughout the movie.

Pure 70s 80s era Spider-man, exactly what I wanted. Fun, Chaotic, good time.

I finally got to see Spider-Man: Brand New Day, and it was probably the best new MCU film in a while. Not only that, but I really enjoyed it. Here's hoping Doomsday can be just as good, if not better.

30. Spider-Man: Brand New Day (2026)

Fantastic. Easily my favorite of the MCU Spider-Man movies. It's right up there with Spider-Man 2. I expected to like it, I didn't expect to come away feeling this strongly. No disrespect to Jon Watts, but Daniel Cretton's directing style shines here. Loved it.
I saw Spider-Man Brand New Day At the movies #spidermanbrandnewday #marvelstudios #phoenixtheatres

In Daredevil, New York City had become a disaster. Total shambles. 

No mention of that in Spider-man Brand New Day. 

Are we back to keeping TV and movie stories separate again?

#MCU #Daredevil

101. Spider-Man: Brand New Day

While I don't know if this is my favorite of the new Spider-Man films, it's definitely the most emotional. The cast is fucking great, especially the villain, the action is fantastic, and it effectively uses other Marvel characters without feeling pandering

So “Spider-Man: Brand New Day” may be my favorite Spider-Man film now. Just might supplant “Spider-Man 2.” Honestly, kinda shocked at how well-written it was, the threads spun and woven and never quite out-of-control. Tight.

What Aunt May says, in the bedroom flashback, rivals the steady speech.

record.text: Yearning, longing glances across a crowded party, letters left for the object of one’s affection to read, chivalrously offering a lady a ride home…Spider-Man: Brand New Day is a Jane Austen novel.

I watched Spider-Man: Brand New Day. It’s good. Best MCU Spider-Man movie. I ranked it #9 in MCU over all.

Still trying to rank it among Spider-Man movies, but I just don’t know where it lands with the 2 spiderverse movies. This is all gut feeling stuff. And my gut says “maybe.”

@mikaelkasurinen.bsky.social hey just came out of the cinema after watching Spider-Man Brand New Day. Did they casually drop 5-10 CONTROL/Quantum Break references in there? I noticed a lot of similarities.

Enjoyed Spider-Man: Brand New Day. It’s basically the same film as Thunderbolts, which is sort of fine because I enjoyed that too. Jon Bernthal doing his Accountant 2 violent comic relief is great (loved every “baaaah!”). Solid Sunday afternoon fun, happy to check out of the MCU again for a while.

I was not expecting to love Spider-Man: Brand New Day as much as I did. Like I knew I was gonna like it but WOW, did I LOVE it. 

Maybe because I’ve been binging the ‘94 cartoon, but it somehow managed to fit in all these characters into one story while still focusing on Peter and it felt natural.
